newsitem.title: USA: Stocks claw back to post gains at midday.
newsitem.headline: Stocks claw back to post gains at midday.

text.p: Stocks climbed back from early losses to move higher Tuesday, helped by a firmer bond market and the agreement between President Clinton and congressional Republicans to balance the federal budget.

Just after 1 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average, which stood lower for much of the morning, rose further into record territory, adding 45.29 points to 8,166.40 after edging higher to another record Monday.
The Nasdaq composite index, laden with high-technology issues, rose 2.01 points to 1,565.54.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a 15-11 margin on the New York Stock Exchange, where volume was moderate at about 302 million shares.

Stocks got a lift from bonds, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury moving out of the loss column and rising fractionally to push its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, down to 6.40 percent from 6.41 percent Monday.
"There was some programme activity in the last half-hour and we have had a turnaround in the bond market," Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said.
Bonds and stocks rebounded as investors continued to buy on dips, analysts said.
Early in the session, investors paused to digest the second-quarter employment cost index and details of the budget accord, announced late Monday.
They also awaited other reports due later in the week, including the first reading on the economy's second-quarter performance, due Thursday, and the July employment report, due Friday.
"The market is taking a bit of breather," said Doug Myers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane. "There is a lot of economic news coming out this week."

Stocks got off to a sluggish start after the Labour Department reported an 0.8 percent rise in the second quarter employment cost index, compared to an 0.6 percent gain in the previous quarter. The report was in line with forecasts.
While analysts said the data showed scant signs of inflation and upward pressure on wages, they said much of the good news had been factored in by investors.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 4.44 points to 940.89.
The American Stock Exchange index fell 1.21 points to 638.14.
